transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-15 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Anna (Redwood AE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Ben (Redwood SE), John (Greenfield CTO), Emily (Head of Security), Raj (PM), Aisha (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): POC scoping — security pilot. Customer needs compliance docs, SSO integration, RBAC, auditability. Discussed pilot success criteria and benchmark plan; Redwood to provide SOC2 artifacts and run perf tests.

00:00:05 Anna: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick intros then dive into security and the pilot scope.
00:00:15 John: Hi, John here, CTO at Greenfield. We're evaluating Redwood for a small clinical notes summarization pilot — security is the big gating factor for us.
00:00:22 Emily: Emily, head of security. I care about SOC 2, ISO if you have it, SSO, RBAC and audit logs. Also we need to understand key management and data residency.
00:00:30 Miguel: Great, thanks. Quick familar note — Miguel SE, I run performance and infra stuff. We'll propose a benchmark plan.
00:00:38 Raj: Raj here, I'll be PMing the pilot and setting success metrics.
00:00:45 Priya: Priya, CSM — I'll coordinate timelines and the onboarding checklist.

00:01:10 Anna: High level agenda: 1) confirm success criteria, 2) workload sizing and benchmarks, 3) security/compliance ask list and what we can deliver for a pilot, 4) timeline and next steps. Any additions?
00:01:20 Emily: No, that's good. Let's start with our must-haves so we don't go down the wrong path.

00:01:40 John: Our success criteria for the pilot: 1) p95 latency under 800ms for 256-token generation on our representative workload; 2) throughput of ~60 reqs/min sustained; 3) outputs meet accuracy thresholds on our internal eval set; 4) no PHI leakage — i.e., logs and model responses can't be used to reconstruct sensitive data.
00:02:05 Miguel: Helpful. When you say "representative workload" can you describe token distribution and prompt shapes?
00:02:10 Raj: Most calls are 64-300 tokens inputs, half short prompts like triage summaries, the other half long notes. We expect peak concurrency around 8-12 concurrent users hitting the system.
00:02:28 Miguel: Ok that maps to a mixed workload — we'll run two benchmark profiles: short prompt low-latency and long-sequence throughput. We'll measure p50/p95/p99, token cost, and CPU/GPU utilization.
00:02:40 Ben: We'll also capture KV cache hit rates — if you have repetition across prompts caching helps a lot.
00:02:48 Aisha: A question on caching: does caching store any patient text in Redis or similar, and how is it encrypted?
00:02:56 Miguel: Good callout. We can use in-memory KV cache inside the cluster (evicted on restart) or an external Redis with AES-256 at rest. For the pilot we can keep cache ephemeral inside a dedicated VPC so it never touches external shared services.
00:03:12 Emily: That leads into KMS: we require CMEK — customer managed encryption keys — or HSM for production. For the pilot, is Redwood offering customer KMS integration?
00:03:22 Anna: Yes, we support KMS integrations. For hosted pilots we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). For private installs we support HSM in the on-prem package. We'll share the integration guide.
00:03:35 Emily: We'll need proof points — SOC 2 report or ISO cert copy and details on what that covers.
00:03:42 Anna: Understood. We'll share our SOC 2 Type II report and the ISO summary pack. Also redacted control mappings.
00:03:50 John: Great. Also SSO — we use Okta and need SAML 2.0 for single sign-on; RBAC mapped to our groups. How fine-grained is RBAC? Can we restrict model access per team and enable audit trail per user?
00:04:05 Ben: Our RBAC supports org / team / role level bindings. You can restrict routes (generate, embeddings), models, and limits at token quotas per API key. Audit logs include user identity for each call when SSO is integrated.
00:04:18 Emily: And those audit logs — are they immutable? We need tamper-evidence for compliance.
00:04:24 Miguel: Logs are written to append-only storage backed by object store with versioning; for private deployments files can be shipped to your SIEM. We can produce signed log digests for tamper evidence on request for an enterprise contract. For pilot we'll provide append-only export and recommend SIEM ingestion.
00:04:40 Raj: On data residency: pilot data will be US-only. Any callouts for hosted regions?
00:04:46 Anna: Our hosted US region is available and we can pin the POC to that region. For Dedicated and Private you can choose on-prem or a VPC deployment in your cloud account.
00:04:56 Emily: Do you support data retention controls — e.g., zero-retention mode for logs and no retention of request vectors?
00:05:05 Ben: We have a retention policy config. For the pilot we can enable a short retention window (24–72 hours) and we can disable persistent training/retention features. We'll note that ephemeral KV/cache is not persisted beyond the instance lifecycle.
00:05:20 John: Ok. Now on benchmarks — Miguel, what will you run and how long?
00:05:25 Miguel: We'll run two benchmark suites: Suite A (short prompts) — 1000 requests at concurrency 8, measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec; Suite B (long prompts) — 500 requests with average 400 tokens, concurrency 4. We'll run each several times at different model configs (full float, 8-bit quant) and report latency, throughput, and token cost. Total time to complete benchmarks ~3 business days once we have access to a test dataset and tokenized samples.
00:05:52 Raj: Do you need synthetic data or can we share a de-identified sample set?
00:05:57 Emily: We prefer de-identified samples but need a DPA in place; for the pilot we can share a small de-id set.
00:06:05 Priya: We'll circulate our standard DPA and the pilot confidentiality addendum after the call.
00:06:12 John: Timeline — we're hoping for a 4-week pilot: week 0 onboarding, week 1 perf and integration, week 2 validation and QA, week 3 stakeholder review and results. Feasible?
00:06:25 Anna: Feasible if we start this month and you provide initial data and Okta access within 3 business days. We'll prioritize.
00:06:32 Miguel: On the infra side we'll need an API key with SSO binding or a service account, and a sandbox VPC if you want dedicated capacity or the private VPN for the on-prem test.
00:06:44 Aisha: We prefer dedicated capacity in our VPC for the pilot to validate network restrictions. Is that supported for short-term pilots?
00:06:51 Ben: Yes, we can provision a small dedicated GPU pool reserved for a pilot (2x A10 equivalent) for the duration; there is a minimum cost but we can propose a pilot pricing tier. I'll share numbers.
00:07:05 Raj: Cost sensitivity: we need ballpark $/1k tokens and cost per hour for the dedicated pool.
00:07:12 Ben: We'll include token cost estimates based on the benchmark results; initial rough is $X per 1k tokens for hosted, and for dedicated it's a fixed hourly plus lower per-token compute. We'll put exact figures in the follow-up.
00:07:28 Emily: Back to compliance — we also run annual external audits; can Redwood provide control mappings to our ISMS?
00:07:36 Anna: Yes, we'll provide control mappings and a short questionnaire template mapping to SOC2 controls and ISO clauses.
00:07:43 Emily: Great. One more question — model privacy and fine-tuning: will my data be used to update shared model weights? We need assurance no training on customer data without opt-in.
00:07:53 Miguel: By default hosted endpoints do not use customer requests for training. For training/continuous learning features we require explicit opt-in and separate contracts. We'll document this clearly.
00:08:05 John: Perfect. Any blockers for the pilot?
00:08:09 Emily: Confirm SAML flow, audit formatting, and KMS integration. Those are blockers.
00:08:15 Anna: We'll prioritize docs for those three items and provide a schedule.
00:08:22 Raj: For the success criteria we also need a quality metric: Rouge-L or F1 threshold on your eval set. We'll include the evaluation harness.
00:08:30 Miguel: We'll run your eval harness against baseline model and suggested quantized variants and report regressions.
00:08:38 Speaker 1: (mumble) also want to check latency from your East Coast region, is there a network hop measurement?
00:08:45 Miguel: We'll include synthetic pings and real-world request latency from your region.
00:08:50 Emily: Another compliance note — can you provide evidence of background checks for ops team accessing customer data?
00:08:58 Anna: We can provide a summary of personnel security controls and the roles with access to customer data; detailed personnel records require an NDA, but we can provide evidence of background check policies.
00:09:12 John: OK, let's lock down the concrete success criteria — I'll read them out and you confirm: 1) p95 < 800ms for 256 tokens, 2) throughput 60 req/min sustained with less than 5% error rate, 3) eval metric >= threshold (we'll send thresholds), 4) no persistence of raw PHI beyond 24 hours in pilot and KMS-managed keys.
00:09:36 Miguel: Confirmed — plus audit logs with user identity and request/response metadata available to Greenfield and exported to your SIEM.
00:09:45 Emily: Also need RBAC mapping so only specific Okta groups can call the generate endpoint.
00:09:51 Ben: That's supported — we'll share RBAC mapping templates.
00:09:56 Priya: I'll capture these as acceptance criteria in the pilot plan and circulate.
00:10:05 Anna: Anything else on security?
00:10:08 Aisha: Network egress restrictions — can we ensure no internet egress from the dedicated pool except to specified endpoints?
00:10:14 Miguel: Yes, in the VPC we can apply egress rules and NAT restrictions; for private on-prem it's entirely under your control.
00:10:22 John: Ok, moving on — timeline and responsibilities recap?
00:10:26 Priya: Action items: Anna to send SOC2/ISO and security docs; Miguel to run benchmarks given tokenized sample; Ben to provide pilot pricing; Priya to send DPA; Customer to provide de-id dataset and Okta admin access. We'll try to start onboarding week of 2027-09-20.
00:10:47 Emily: Can we get a draft SAML metadata exchange today or tomorrow?
00:10:51 Anna: Yes we'll send the SAML metadata and an example assertion mapping by EOD tomorrow.
00:10:58 Raj: For the benchmarks, how will we share results? Spreadsheet?
00:11:02 Miguel: We'll upload a benchmark sheet to the shared drive and include raw traces. Link will be included in the follow-up.
00:11:10 John: Any risk of model fallback changing during pilot? E.g., if a node goes down will you failover to a different model variant and could that affect accuracy?
00:11:20 Ben: We have deterministic fallback policies; for pilot we can pin the model version to avoid silent changes. If fallback occurs we can route to a pinned compatible variant and note the change in audit logs.
00:11:34 Emily: Will fallback be visible in the audit logs?
00:11:37 Miguel: Yes, we'll include reason codes (node failure, capacity) in the logs.
00:11:42 John: Sounds good.
00:11:50 Speaker 2: (crosstalk) okay final question on retention of logs in hosted vs dedicated?
00:11:55 Ben: Hosted: we can configure retention windows per customer and export to your SIEM; Dedicated: you control retention in your VPC.
00:12:04 Anna: Closing out, thanks all. We'll follow-up with the package: SOC2, ISO summary, SAML metadata, RBAC template, pilot pricing, benchmark plan. Expect emails by Thursday.
00:12:18 Emily: Appreciate it.
00:12:22 John: Thanks everyone.

(There is a short second half of more detailed technical clarifications:)
00:25:03 Miguel: Deep-dive note: our runtime supports KV cache segmentation by tenant and by model shard, we can enable per-customer namespaces to ensure no cross-tenant leakage.
00:25:20 Aisha: If there's a crash, how do you guarantee ephemeral cache doesn't get persisted to disk?
00:25:27 Miguel: We run cache in tmpfs for dedicated pools; on crash the kernel will drop it. For extra assurance we can schedule a daily shred job for any persisted artifacts and produce a proof of deletion for pilot.
00:25:39 Emily: For audit format, we prefer JSON lines with timestamp, user_id, request_id, model_version, action, and outcome. Can Redwood support that?
00:25:47 Ben: Yes, that's our default schema; we'll send an example log file format.
00:25:55 Raj: Regarding SSO groups mapping to RBAC, can the mapping be automated via SCIM?
00:25:59 Anna: We support SCIM provisioning for Okta and can map groups to RBAC roles. For the pilot we can do manual mapping and expand to SCIM if you want automated sync.
00:26:08 John: Ok final check on timeline — we agreed pilot kickoff next Tuesday, benchmarks done by end of next week, interim check-in after 10 days, final review week 4.
00:26:18 Priya: I'll send invites now.
00:26:22 Anna: Thanks team, talk soon.

Transcript end.
